heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to EOR & PEO in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for EOR & PEO in Ecuador.

steps.title: Core vs Complementary
steps.description: Mandato 8 prohibits outsourcing 'core' business activities. EOR is legal only for specialized services not central to the local entity's main purpose.

steps.title: Joint Liability
steps.description: The client company is jointly liable (Responsabilidad Solidaria) for all labor obligations if the EOR fails to pay.

steps.title: Direct Hire Preference
steps.description: Ecuadorian law strongly favors direct employment. Long-term EOR arrangements can be reclassified as direct employment by courts.

items.title: Permanent Establishment
items.text: Having senior managers or sales agents acting through an EOR can trigger PE status for the foreign parent company.

items.title: Employee Tenure
items.text: Employees often prefer direct hires due to job security perception. EORs are seen as temporary.

items.title: Benefits Parity
items.text: Ensure EOR employees receive the same statutory benefits (13th/14th/Profits) as they would if hired directly.

steps.title: KYC & MSA
steps.description: Client passes compliance checks and signs Master Services Agreement (1-3 Days).

steps.title: Employee Data Collection
steps.description: Provider collects bank details, ID copies, and beneficiary info (1-2 Days).

steps.title: Contract Registration
steps.description: Contract is signed and registered with SUT (Ministry of Labor) (1 Day).

steps.title: IESS Affiliation
steps.description: Employee is affiliated with Social Security from Day 1 (Immediate).

faqs.question: Is EOR 100% legal?
faqs.answer: It operates in a gray area under 'Prestación de Servicios Especializados'. Indefinite use for core roles acts against Mandato 8 spirit.

faqs.question: Can we terminate at will?
faqs.answer: No. 'Despido Intempestivo' (Unjustified Dismissal) carries a penalty of 1 year of salary (if <3 years tenure) or more.

faqs.question: What is the probation period?
faqs.answer: 90 days maximum. Termination during this period is penalty-free.

faqs.question: Does EOR cover profit sharing?
faqs.answer: Yes, legally the EOR is the employer and must distribute its profits. However, since EORs have low margins/profits per head, this creates disparity.

rows.label: Reserve Fund
values: Payable monthly or yearly after Year 1.

steps.title: 13th Salary (Bono Navideño)
steps.description: One month's salary paid by Dec 24th. Tax-free.

steps.title: 14th Salary (Bono Escolar)
steps.description: One Unified Basic Salary (SBU, $460 in 2025). Paid in March (Coast) or August (Sierra).

steps.title: 15% Profit Sharing
steps.description: 15% of net pre-tax profits must be distributed. 10% to all employees, 5% based on family dependents.

items.title: Check Payments
items.text: Paying salaries by check is outdated and legally risky. Direct bank transfer is the standard proof of payment.

items.title: Combined Accounts
items.text: Payroll payments are often done via 'Cash Management' files uploaded to banks like Pichincha, Produbanco, or Guayaquil.

items.title: Currency (USD)
items.text: Ecuador uses the US Dollar. No FX conversion is needed for US companies, simplifying payroll funding.

steps.title: Update Novelties
steps.description: Report overtime, vacations, and sick leave by the 25th of the month.

steps.title: Calculate Provisions
steps.description: Accrue 13th, 14th, and Vacation portions to avoid cash flow shock in Dec/Apr.

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Pay net salary to employees by the last working day of the month/start of next.

steps.title: IESS Payment
steps.description: Submit employer/employee contributions to IESS by the 15th of the following month.

faqs.question: What is the 2025 Minimum Wage?
faqs.answer: USD $460.00 per month (SBU).

faqs.question: Is profit sharing capped?
faqs.answer: Yes, the individual distribution is capped at 24 times the Unified Basic Salary (SBU).

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: 13th and 14th salaries are exempt from Income Tax and IESS contributions.

faqs.question: What about overtime?
faqs.answer: Saturdays/Sundays are 100% surcharge. Weeknight overtime is 50%. Night shift (7pm-6am) has a 25% surcharge.

steps.title: Start with Base
steps.description: Identify Unified Basic Salary (SBU) or contracted monthly salary.

steps.title: Add Overtime
steps.description: Calculate 50% or 100% surcharges based on hours worked.

steps.title: Deduct IESS
steps.description: Subtract 9.45% (Employee Contribution) from the total income.

steps.title: Deduct Tax
steps.description: Apply Income Tax (Impuesto a la Renta) withholding based on the annual projection.

items.title: 15% Profit Sharing
items.text: Not included in the monthly calc. Companies must distribute 15% of annual pre-tax profits to employees in April.

items.title: Vacation
items.text: 15 days per year (standard). After 5 years, add 1 day per year. Unused vacation is paid out upon termination.

items.title: Reserve Fund
items.text: 8.33% monthly or accumulated. Must be paid directly to IESS or the employee (if requested).

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.text: 12 weeks paid. Employer pays 25%, IESS pays 75%. If IESS liability exists, Employer pays 100%.

items.title: Paternity Leave
items.text: 10 days paid (optional extension to 15 days in special cases).

items.title: Severance Risk
items.text: Unjustified dismissal indemnification is high, deterring casual firing.

faqs.question: Can I pay in crypto?
faqs.answer: No. Salaries must be paid in legal tender (USD) via the financial system.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: IESS is mandatory. Private health insurance is optional but common as a benefit.

faqs.question: How do I calculate severance?
faqs.answer: It depends on the cause. Unjustified dismissal is expensive (1 year salary min). Resignation (Desahucio) gets 25% of monthly salary per year served.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Ecuador.

items.title: Zero Minimum Capital
items.text: SAS (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) can be formed with $0 capital, though $400 is recommended for banks.

items.title: Digital Formation
items.text: Can be constituted via private document (no notary deed required), saving ~USD $500-800 in fees.

items.title: One Shareholder
items.text: Unlike traditional S.A.s, an SAS can be owned by a single person (Foreign or Local).

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Reserve name with Superintendencia de Compañías (online).

steps.title: Constitutive Act
steps.description: Draft private bylaws appointing the Legal Representative (must be resident or foreign with Ecuador visa).

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register the SAS with the Superintendencia's Mercantile Registry.

steps.title: Obtain RUC
steps.description: Register with SRI (Tax Authority) to get the tax ID (RUC).

steps.title: IESS Employer ID
steps.description: Register as an employer with the Social Security Institute.

rows.label: Legal Fees (Lawyer)
values: For drafting bylaws and handling filings.

rows.label: Notary/Registry
values: Minimal for SAS. Higher for S.A.

items.title: Apostille
items.text: Foreign shareholder documents (Power of Attorney, Good Standing) must be apostilled in the home country.

items.title: Translation
items.text: Documents not in Spanish must be translated by an accredited translator in Ecuador.

items.title: Visa
items.text: The foreign Legal Rep needs a temporary residence visa (Mercosur or Professional) to sign the RUC.

faqs.question: Do I need a resident director?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Legal Representative must be an Ecuadorian citizen or a foreigner with a valid residency visa.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: SAS incorporation is fast—typically 2-4 weeks. Traditional S.A.s take 6-8 weeks.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the RUC and municipal patent (Patente Municipal), a local fiscal address is required.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account online?
faqs.answer: Partially. You can start the process, but the Legal Rep usually must sign in person at the bank.

heroData.title: Staffing in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Ecuador.

steps.title: SUT Registration
steps.description: Contracts must be registered in the 'Sistema Único de Trabajo' (SUT) of the Ministry of Labor within 30 days.

steps.title: Probation Period
steps.description: Fixed at 90 days. Must be explicitly stated in the written contract.

steps.title: Foreign Quota
steps.description: At least 80% of the workforce must be Ecuadorian. Foreign hires need valid visas.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text: Ecuadorian business culture is hierarchical. Decisions are typically made by the top executive.

items.title: Punctuality
items.text: While deadlines are important, meeting start times can be flexible ('Hora Ecuatoriana'). Be patient.

items.title: Termination
items.text: Firing is difficult. Documentation of poor performance (memos) is critical for a 'Visto Bueno' case.

steps.title: Indefinite Contract
steps.description: The standard form. Can only be terminated for cause or with indemnification.

steps.title: Special Types
steps.description: Productive, Tourist, and Entrepreneurial contracts offered more flexibility but have specific sector requirements.

steps.title: Telework
steps.description: Legally recognized. Requires an addendum specifying equipment provision and disconnection rights.

faqs.question: What is 'Visto Bueno'?
faqs.answer: A procedure to request government approval for firing an employee for 'Just Cause' (e.g., absenteeism, insubordination).

faqs.question: Is background checking legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, requesting judicial records (Récord Policial) is common, but discrimination based on it is prohibited.

faqs.question: Can I use fixed-term contracts?
faqs.answer: Strictly limited to temporary, occasional, or seasonal needs. Indefinite contracts are the default mandated by law.

faqs.question: Are 13th/14th salaries mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, absolutely. They can be paid monthly (acumulado) if the employee requests it in writing.

rows.label: Coworking Desk
values: Monthly hot desk in major cities.

heroData.title: HRIS in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for HRIS in Ecuador.

items.title: Biometric Consent
items.text: Under LOPDP, biometrics are 'Sensitive Data'. Employers must obtain explicit, free, and informed consent. Coercion (fear of job loss) invalidates consent.

items.title: Impact Assessment
items.text: A 'Evaluación de Impacto de Protección de Datos' (EIPD) is mandatory before implementing invasive monitoring systems.

items.title: Employee Rights
items.text: Employees have the right to access, rectify, delete, and oppose data processing (ARCO rights).

steps.title: Requirements Gathering
steps.description: Define scope: Payroll, Time Tracking, Performance Mgmt, etc.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Choose between local (compliant with SRI/IESS) or global vendors (integrations).

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Migrate employee master data. Ensure LOPDP compliance during transfer.

steps.title: User Training
steps.description: Train HR admins and employees on self-service portals.

items.title: Disconnect Right
items.text: Employees have the right to disconnect outside working hours. HRIS notification settings must respect this.

items.title: IESS Integration
items.text: Local payroll/HR systems often output 'Planillas' in the specific .txt format required for IESS uploads.

items.title: Audit Trails
items.text: HRIS systems must maintain immutable logs of all data access and modifications to demonstrate LOPDP compliance.

faqs.question: Can I use fingerprint scanners for attendance?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must offer a non-biometric alternative (e.g., ID card) to ensure consent is truly free.

faqs.question: Where is data stored?
faqs.answer: Cross-border transfer requires adequacy decisions or standard contractual clauses approved by the Superintendence.

faqs.question: What are the penalties?
faqs.answer: Fines can reach up to 1% of annual turnover for severe infractions.

heroData.title: Accounting in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Accounting in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Accounting in Ecuador.

items.title: NIIF (IFRS)
items.text: Ecuador mandates International Financial Reporting Standards (NIIF) for all companies overseen by the Superintendencia.

items.title: E-Invoicing
items.text: Electronic invoicing is mandatory. From Aug 2025, stricter rules apply to cancelling issued invoices.

items.title: Currency
items.text: Books must be kept in US Dollars. Spanish is the official language for accounting records.

steps.title: REBEFICS (UBO Report)
steps.description: Due in February (dates vary by RUC 9th digit).

steps.title: Profit Sharing Payment
steps.description: Must be paid to employees by April 15th.

steps.title: Annual Tax Return
steps.description: Form 101 (Corporate Income Tax) is due in April.

steps.title: SuperCías Financials
steps.description: Full financial statements must be uploaded to the Superintendencia portal by April 30th.

items.title: Retention Period
items.text: Accounting records and supporting documents must be kept for 7 years.

items.title: External Audit
items.text: Mandatory for companies with assets >$500k. Auditor must be appointed by the Shareholders' Meeting.

items.title: Language
items.text: All accounting records must be maintained in Spanish and denominated in US Dollars.

faqs.question: Can I offshore accounting?
faqs.answer: Partial processing yes, but the Accountant signing the returns must be an Ecuadorian CPA (Contador Público Autorizado).

faqs.question: Is software mandatory?
faqs.answer: Not legally, but practically required for E-Invoicing and generating XMLs for SRI.

faqs.question: What is 'Anexo Transaccional'?
faqs.answer: A monthly report detailing all purchases, sales, withholdings, and exports, submitted to SRI.

items.title: Superintendencia de Compañías
items.text: The primary regulator for all corporate entities. Oversees financial reporting and UBO compliance.

items.title: UAFE Reporting
items.text: Construction, Automotive, and Legal sectors must report monthly to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAFE) to prevent money laundering.

items.title: Electronic Mailbox
items.text: Maintain an active email address registered with the Superintendencia; legal notices are served digitally.

steps.title: Who must file?
steps.description: All companies (SAS, S.A., Cía. Ltda) and foreign branches.

steps.title: What to report?
steps.description: Full chain of ownership up to the natural person (Ultimate Beneficial Owner).

steps.title: Deadline
steps.description: Annually in February. Late filing triggers heavy fines and the 28% CIT rate penalty.

items.title: Shareholders Meeting
items.text: Must be held by March 31st each year to approve financial statements.

items.title: Municipal Patents
items.text: Payable to the local municipality (e.g., Quito/Guayaquil) by May.

items.title: Updates
items.text: Update the Legal Representative or Address in the Mercantile Registry immediately upon change.

faqs.question: What is UAFE?
faqs.answer: The Financial Analysis Unit. Real estate, auto dealers, and lawyers must report suspicious transactions for AML.

faqs.question: Is a resident legal rep mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Foreign owners must appoint a resident (national or visa holder) to face the SRI and SuperCías.

faqs.question: Does the Legal Rep have liability?
faqs.answer: Yes, they are civilly and criminally liable for the company's tax and labor obligations.

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
values: Standard rate. Can rise to 28% if UBOs are hidden.

rows.label: Dividend Withholding
values: Standard withholding on dividends to non-residents.

rows.label: Currency Outflow (ISD)
values: Impuesto a la Salida de Divisas (varies by sector/policy).

steps.title: Monthly Declarations
steps.description: VAT and Withholdings (Form 104 and 103) are due monthly based on the 9th digit of the RUC.

steps.title: Dividend Reporting
steps.description: ADI (Anexo de Dividendos) must be filed annually reporting distributed profits.

steps.title: Income Tax Prep
steps.description: Calculate tax reconciliation (Conciliación Tributaria) to determine deductible/non-deductible expenses.

steps.title: Payment
steps.description: CIT payment is due in April. Can be paid in installments if authorized.

items.title: Investment Contracts
items.text: Companies investing >$1M can sign an Investment Contract with the state to freeze tax rules/rates for 15 years.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Transactions with related parties abroad >$3M require a comprehensive TP Report.

items.title: Double Taxation
items.text: Ecuador has treaties (CDIs) with Canada, France, Germany, Spain, etc., allowing reduced withholding rates.

items.title: Non-Deductibles
items.text: Expenses without proper electronic invoices or withholdings are non-deductible and increase the effective tax rate.

items.title: Bancarization
items.text: Payments >$1000 must use the baking system to be deductible. Cash payments are disallowed.

items.title: Late Filing
items.text: Late tax filings attract immediate interest and fines, and repeated offences can lead to closure.

faqs.question: Why 28% CIT?
faqs.answer: The rate increases +3% if the company has shareholders in tax havens or fails to report UBOs (REBEFICS).

faqs.question: Is tech VAT exempt?
faqs.answer: Some digital services were targeted, but verify specific exemptions. Generally, 15% applies.

faqs.question: What is ISD?
faqs.answer: Tax on Currency Outflows. It applies when transferring money abroad. Rates have been fluctuating but generally around 3.5-5%.

faqs.question: Are there local taxes?
faqs.answer: Yes, Municipal Patents (Patente) and the 1.5 per thousand tax on total assets are paid to the local municipality.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to MSA & Legal in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for MSA & Legal in Ecuador.

steps.title: Drafting
steps.description: Draft contracts in Spanish (mandatory) and English (for HQ reference). Prevailing version is Spanish.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: Local legal counsel reviews for Labor Code compliance (non-waivable rights).

steps.title: Signing
steps.description: Sign via wet ink or Certified Digital Signature (Token/Cloud).

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register labor contracts on the SUT platform within 30 days.

items.title: Indefinite Term
items.text: This is the default. Fixed-term contracts (Plazo Fijo) only apply to specific temporary needs.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Must be explicitly stated (90 days). If not written, the contract is deemed indefinite from Day 1.

items.title: IP Assignment
items.text: Include a 'Cesión de Derechos' clause to ensure work product belongs to the employer.

items.title: Indefinite Term
items.text: Specify 'Indefinite Term' (default) or justify 'Fixed Term' strictly.

items.title: Data Protection
items.text: Include a specific Data Protection Clause (LOPDP consent) in all contracts.

items.title: Arbitration
items.text: Arbitration Clause (Mediation Center) is recommended for commercial B2B to avoid slow local courts.

faqs.question: Are digital signatures valid on contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, if using a 'Firma Electrónica Calificada' from an authorized certifier.

faqs.question: Can I agree to foreign law?
faqs.answer: For labor contracts, No. Ecuadorian Labor Code is non-waivable. For B2B, yes, but local enforcement may require homologation.

faqs.question: What is 'Desahucio'?
faqs.answer: Termination notice. Historically applied to both, but recent rulings restrict it in public sector. In private, it usually implies a 25% bonus.

faqs.question: Is arbitration binding?
faqs.answer: Yes, Ecuador respects arbitration clauses if they designate a recognized center (e.g., Chamber of Commerce).

heroData.title: Software in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Software in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Software in Ecuador.

steps.title: Needs Assessment
steps.description: Identify if software needs local tax compliance (e-invoicing) features.

steps.title: Vendor Vetting
steps.description: Verify local support and integration with SRI webservices.

steps.title: Implementation
steps.description: Set up digital certificates (.p12 files) for signing XMLs.

steps.title: Testing
steps.description: Run test environment (Pruebas) with SRI before Production (Producción).

rows.label: Registro Civil / BCE
values: Standard for all public filings (SRI, SuperCías).

items.title: Local vs Global
items.text: Global ERPs (SAP, Oracle) often need a 'Localisation Partner' to handle Ecuadorian tax reporting.

items.title: SaaS Taxation
items.text: Payments for foreign software licenses are subject to 25% withholding tax unless a Double Taxation Treaty applies.

items.title: Data Localization
items.text: While strict data localization isn't mandated, sensitive financial data is best stored with latency in mind.

items.title: Accounting
items.text: Contifico and Dora are popular local cloud-based accounting platforms for SMEs.

items.title: Payroll
items.text: Paradiso and Novit are widely used for local payroll processing.

items.title: CRM
items.text: Global tools like HubSpot and Salesforce are widely adopted, though local support may be limited.

faqs.question: Is e-signature mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the Legal Representative to sign tax returns and corporate filings.

faqs.question: What is the 'Token'?
faqs.answer: A physical USB device. Most modern use is the 'Archivo' (.p12) format which is more flexible.

faqs.question: Can I use Docusign?
faqs.answer: For private agreements, yes. For government filings, no—you need a local 'Firma Electrónica'.

heroData.title: Marketing in Ecuador
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Marketing in Ecuador
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Marketing in Ecuador.

steps.title: Audience Definition
steps.description: Regional differences are key (Costa vs. Sierra culture).

steps.title: Channel Selection
steps.description: Prioritize Facebook and TikTok for B2C; LinkedIn for B2B.

steps.title: Localization
steps.description: Use local slang ('modismos') carefully. Ecuadorian Spanish is neutral but has regional variations.

steps.title: Compliance
steps.description: Ensure ads respect Consumer Protection Law (no misleading claims).

items.title: Influencer Tax
items.text: Influencers must issue invoices and are subject to income tax. Barter deals are also taxable events in theory.

items.title: Social Commerce
items.text: WhatsApp and TikTok are dominant sales channels in Ecuador, often outperforming traditional web e-commerce.

items.title: Data Privacy
items.text: Marketing emails require opt-in consent under LOPDP.

items.title: Facebook
items.text: Still the most widely used platform across all demographics.

items.title: TikTok
items.text: Exploding growth, especially for younger demographics and viral trends.

items.title: Instagram
items.text: Essential for lifestyle branding and reaching urban millennials.

faqs.question: Can I advertise in English?
faqs.answer: It is better to use Spanish. English proficiency is low outside of top-tier professionals.

faqs.question: Are there restrictions?
faqs.answer: Alcohol and tobacco advertising is heavily regulated/prohibited in mass media.

faqs.question: What is the VAT on ads?
faqs.answer: 15%. Digital ads purchased from abroad (e.g., Meta Ads) also attract 5% ISD and potentially VAT.
